summary: Field-Shift is a decision-support tool designed to help farmers pick their crop rotation. It uses NASA Earth observation data to guide these choices. Farmers input details about their farm and the current crop rotation. Field-Shift then evaluates at three strategies, including the one they are already using. It compares them using NASA POWER climate data along with Earth observation data like soil moisture and vegetation indices. The results are ranked based on what matters to the farmer—things like profit, water use, soil health or climate risk. The demo shows a farm near Coimbatore in Tamil Nadu. The app runs completely on -fetched static data so it loads quickly and does not need a backend. All the text is stored in a translations file making it easy to add Tamil. Field-Shift turns satellite data into side-by-side recommendations for crop rotation. It helps farmers move away from decisions made by habit and, toward data-driven choices.
details:
FieldShift helps farmers compare crop rotation options for the place they farm. They enter the two crops they currently grow, add what they know about their soil and water, and choose what matters most to them, such as saving water or protecting soil. The app compares the current rotation with other options and explains what influenced each result.

FieldShift uses NASA POWER climate records, GPM rainfall estimates and, when available, SMAP soil moisture data. It also draws on SoilGrids, MODIS, elevation data and a global crop calendar. The app summarizes past climate patterns and shows how much the results vary. These records can help people discuss possible choices, but they cannot predict a harvest or replace local knowledge. Map layers provide a wider regional view, not measurements of an individual field.

We built FieldShift with JavaScript, React and Vite. It uses Leaflet and Google Maps/Places for maps and location search, and Recharts for climate charts. The app runs in a browser and is hosted on GitHub Pages.

Our goal is to make climate information easier to use in conversations between farmers and local advisors. Farmers can see why an option scored well or poorly and which details still need checking, such as crop calendars, soil tests, water access or local prices. FieldShift is an early decision-support tool, so its crop assumptions and scoring rules still need to be reviewed with farmers and agricultural experts.
